newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain links cooperation with Cuba to reforms.
newsitem.headline: Spain links cooperation with Cuba to reforms.

text.p: Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Thursday cooperation with Cuba should be linked to political and economic reforms.

Matutes said in a radio interview pressure should applied to encourage Cuban President Fidel Castro to spearhead change, a call certain to please the United States which has been urging linkage of trade with Cuba to democratic reforms.

"Spanish help and cooperation must be linked to reforms, like the release of political prisoners or the start of a minimum of economic liberalisation, although this will be a long-term process," said Matutes.
"We won't achieve this if we don't apply a little pressure to encourage him (Castro) to make these reforms. We are looking for a peaceful transition led by Castro himself."

Spain and Cuba have had close ties historically. But the new conservative government led by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar broke with its Socialist predecessor and took a tougher line on Cuba, aligning itself more closely with Washington.
Aznar's government has said it intends to cease all non-humanitarian aid to Cuba.
Spain is a leading investor in Cuba and, in line with European Union policy, opposes the U.S. Helms Burton law which penalises foreign firms investing in Cuba.
